query: In `tools/pdf2txt.py`, explain how `extract_text` drives the conversion: what it requires from the caller, how the output type is decided from the output file name, and how its behaviour differs between writing to standard output and writing to a file.

operations.name: Calling it without input files is an error
expressions: raise PDFValueError("Must provide files to work upon!")

operations.name: The output type is overridden by the output file's extension
Writing to standard output uses the stdout stream
Standard output forces the UTF-8 codec
Writing to a file opens the output in binary mode

dependencies.name: The extension override only applies when the default text type is in use and the output is a file
The override is chosen by matching the file name suffix
A dash as the output file name selects the standard output path
The codec is forced only when standard output reports an encoding
